builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CARE-PO: Controllable Tool-Call Efficiency for LLM Agents
summary: CARE-PO replaces GRPO efficiency rewards that price tool calls against the policy's own rollouts (which drift and can collapse to zero calls) with a fixed difficulty-anchored budget, injected successful trajectories, and an effort tag in the prompt to select an operating point. It costs an online RL training run (GRPO) over tool-use trajectories, plus curated successful trajectories and per-task difficulty budgets, which is beyond typical constrained-infrastructure budgets for anything but small models. Failure modes include size-dependent generalization: at 9B both operating points sacrifice success rate for fewer calls on held-out multi-hop benchmarks, and the method depends on reliable difficulty estimates and success labels.
rationale: The method requires online RL training of tool-use agents with curated data, which exceeds the reader's no-foundation-training, limited-budget constraints, though the prompt-level effort-tag idea and the cost diagnosis are worth tracking.
technique: Anchored efficiency rewards with effort-tagged prompting for tool agents

claims.statement: CARE-PO replaces GRPO efficiency rewards that price tool calls against the policy's own rollouts (which drift and can collapse to zero calls) with a fixed difficulty-anchored budget, injected successful trajectories, and an effort tag in the prompt to select an operating point. It costs an online RL training run (GRPO) over tool-use trajectories, plus curated successful trajectories and per-task difficulty budgets, which is beyond typical constrained-infrastructure budgets for anything but small models. Failure modes include size-dependent generalization: at 9B both operating points sacrifice success rate for fewer calls on held-out multi-hop benchmarks, and the method depends on reliable difficulty estimates and success labels.
Five of six operating points across three model sizes improve on the base model in both success rate and tool-call count on GAIA; call count stays well above zero during training, avoiding collapse.
